title: Rolling resistance slows a rolling wheel
summary: Rolling resistance is the set of forces that impede a rolling wheel, so a roll does not go on unchanged.
body: OpenStax Physics lists rolling resistance beside kinetic friction, static friction, and drag. It says rolling resistance impedes the rolling of a wheel. The key-term sense on the first-law page is a resistance to motion that slows things down. A ball or wheel on a floor therefore keeps going only until those forces, or some other net force, change the motion. The book does not claim a real floor is frictionless. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020.
